equivalents.note: The Tibetan takes māṅga as the stern of the boat (gru yi mjug), where Munidatta has mārga, 'path'; at 5a it takes māgā as the prow (gru sna).
The Tibetan reads māgā as the prow (gru sna) and has the rower climb onto it (zhon), a verb the Bengali half-line lacks, so pairing it with the stern of 4a; Munidatta has mārga, 'path'.

The Tibetan has 'north and south' (byang dang lho), taking dāhiṇa in its other sense, 'south', while its commentary at cp.08.m5 quotes this phrase and then glosses it g.yon dang g.yas, 'left and right'.

The Tibetan makes it 'the companion of great bliss' (bde ba chen po'i grogs), in line with Munidatta's mahāsukhasaṅga, where the Bengali may mean great bliss itself met as a companion; cp.08.m5 also has grogs.
lam also renders Munidatta's mārga, 'path', in cp.08.m4 and cp.08.m5, so the Tibetan does not separate the song's road from his path.
rmongs pa is also this translation's word for moha, 'delusion', so it cannot stand for 'fool' alone.
In the Bodhicaryāvatāra verse chu bo che renders mahānadī, 'great river'; elsewhere this translation also uses chu klung for 'river'.
In the Apratiṣṭhānaprakāśa verse paramasukhakaraḥ becomes mchog tu bde bar byed pa, 'making supremely blissful'.

The Tibetan has gzugs kyi rgyan, 'ornament of form', which looks like a rendering of rūpaka, 'metaphor', rather than utprekṣā, and it takes the following -paraṃ as 'to others' (gzhan la rtogs par bya).
The Tibetan renders 'for lack of the guru's lineage' (gurorasampradāyāt) as 'being without the guru's instruction' (bla ma'i gdams pa dang bral bas).
Munidatta's Tibetan cites the word as gru'i mjug, 'stern', yet renders his gloss mārga as lam, 'path' (dga' bral gyi lam), so the two readings stand side by side.

The Tibetan names him nag po spyod pa pa and adds glu dbyangs, 'song', to the attribution; earlier in the segment it also turns Munidatta's caryāpādaḥ into nag po spyod pa'i glu dbyangs, 'the song of Nag po spyod pa', ascribing that quotation to Kāṇha as well.
pavipaṅkajasukha becomes rdo rje dang chu skyes kyi bde ba, 'the bliss of vajra and lotus'.
The Tibetan has only dbus su, 'into the middle', not a channel name such as dbu ma.
Here the Tibetan has sna tshogs pa'i dga' ba, 'joy of variety' (as if vicitrānanda), where cp.08.m4 renders viramānanda as dga' bral.

questions: p-kambala, cp.08.3b: not matched. The Bengali has bāhatu kāmali, 'row, Kāmali', but the Tibetan (bla ma dam pa la dris pa yis 'gro, 'goes by asking the true guru') has no name, only 'goes' ('gro), so the poet's self-naming is missing from the Tibetan of this line (it is present at 2a as la ba pa).

para, cp.08.4b: not matched. The Tibetan (gru skya med par mnyen pa gang gis 'gro, 'with no oar, by what ferryman does it go?') has no word for the far bank, and 'gro, 'goes', is too general to count. The Bengali pāraa may be the verb 'can, is able' (pār-) rather than pāra, 'across', in which case the automatic match is a false one. mnyen pa, 'ferryman', has no clear counterpart in the Bengali.

citta, cp.08.m3: not matched. The Tibetan has bla na med pa'i chos mngon sum du byed par 'gyur, 'comes to make the unsurpassed dharma manifest', with no word for mind. This supports Shastri's correction of …sākṣātvāṭikācitto to -tve, i.e. a form of sākṣātkāritva, 'making manifest', so the apparent citta is probably not a word here and the automatic match should be dropped.

carya, cp.08.m4 (listed as already matched): please check. The spyod pa'i found there is part of the name in nag po spyod pa'i glu dbyangs, 'the song of Nag po spyod pa', which is how the Tibetan renders Munidatta's caryāpādaḥ. It does not render the word 'conduct' on its own.

Possible missed term, cp.08.2a: ubesem̐ in gaaṇa ubesem̐ might be upadeśa, 'instruction' (glossary upadesa), or upaveśa, 'sitting'; the input does not list it. The Tibetan has nam mkha' bltas nas, 'having looked at the sky', with no word for instruction, so no equivalent is given.
